edges.description: The circumscribed benign fibroepithelial tumor presents clinically as a palpable breast lump or mass.

nodes.description: Coordinated proliferation of stromal and epithelial mammary components produces a circumscribed benign fibroepithelial tumor. The stromal component is clonal and commonly MED12-mutant, whereas the accompanying epithelium does not carry the mutation.

Fibroadenoma of the breast is a common cause of a benign breast lump in premenopausal women.

nodes.description: MED12-mutant fibroadenoma stroma has dysregulated estrogen signaling and extracellular-matrix organization. These altered stromal programs provide a plausible hormone-responsive microenvironment for formation of the biphasic lesion, although the intervening paracrine mechanisms remain incompletely resolved.

evidence.snippet: Expression profiling of MED12-mutated and wild-type fibroadenomas revealed that MED12 mutations are associated with dysregulated estrogen signaling and extracellular matrix organization.

meta.association: Somatic driver mutation in most conventional fibroadenomas

evidence.reference_title: MED12 somatic mutations in fibroadenomas and phyllodes tumours of the breast.
evidence.snippet: Somatic mutations in exon 2 of the mediator complex subunit 12 (MED12) gene have been identified in 60% of breast fibroadenomas (FAs).

nodes.description: Recurrent somatic MED12 exon-2 mutations are the principal known driver of conventional breast fibroadenomas. They occur in approximately 59%-65% of tumors and are restricted to the neoplastic stromal rather than epithelial component, establishing fibroadenoma as a stromally driven biphasic lesion.
